items.title: 63477_Joe Darensbourg oral history interview
items.q: this Charlie Moseley, the sax-tenor man that was with us, was an excellent musician.

ctx.x: Well, the two instrumentals, "Ory's Creole Trombone" and (what's the other one...?) "Crooked Blues," I think it is... "Ory's Creole Trombone" is pretty much as they played it all through, even through the revival days, whenever Ory could make it. But the other one, "Crooked Blues," is very sort of orchestrated, and it sounds very much different from, like, the Joe Oliver records of the time, which are much more head stuff, you know. What I'm getting at is, you hadn't worked with Ory up to this time, but you had…

He... Not really. Mutt was about at that time reading in the class that I was. Now, L.Z. Cooper could read pretty good, and this Charlie Moseley, the sax-tenor man that was with us, was an excellent musician. And so far as Alex Hill, he was one of the top arrangers.
I was going to say, he was one of the top musicians.
